title: Baseline organic pollution had no clear link to later annual thermal response at 217 English river sites
abstract: We tested whether early organic pollution predicts later annual thermal response in English river invertebrates. We used 3,715 autumn samples at 217 sites and 79 family labels. Thermal composition directions were trained on 1991-2000 records in other site folds. The later model used baseline log BOD as a continuous modifier, with site, month, region-year and modifier-year effects, current chemistry and survey date. The upper-minus-lower baseline BOD quartile slope difference was -0.0145 score units per air temperature C, with a conditional 95% interval of -0.0550 to +0.0260. Habitat interactions gave -0.0195 (-0.0713 to +0.0324). A site bootstrap that refitted the axes gave -0.0538 to +0.0215 for the main difference. Time-half estimates had opposite signs. These data give no clear evidence that baseline BOD sets the annual thermal response. This null result does not establish equivalence, a pollution-control effect or a cause of the long-term tracking gap. Air temperature, family records, selected sites, baseline-state measurement and incomplete uncertainty remain limits. Source records overlap prior river studies. Code, aggregate results, an original figure and exact external input hashes support reproduction; external databases are not bundled.

display.caption: Annual thermal slopes at baseline BOD quartiles and their difference. Blue lines show conditional cluster intervals. Orange lines show site-bootstrap ranges with axis refitting; years and baseline means remain fixed.
